_note: Structural at-a-glance facts for Bangalore's urban water supply, anchored on the JICA Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Project (Phase 3) Final Report (November 2017, NJS Consultants Co., Ltd, JR(SAEI) 17-063). JICA Phase 3 IS the engineering preparatory survey equivalent to Chennai's ADB CCRWSSP IEE and Madurai's ADB TNUFIP Tranche 2 IEE - same level of engineering depth, same purpose (feasibility evaluation for a sovereign loan), same status as primary citable engineering document. Numbers below are extracted from JICA Phase 3 Final Report (Main Report Part 1, Executive Summary + Chapter 3) unless otherwise noted. Engineering snapshot is 2015-2017; current state notes flagged where the picture has changed since (Stage V commissioned 16 Oct 2024, GBA replaced BBMP 15 May 2025, 369-ward delimitation notified 19 Nov 2025).

_view_overrides.subtitle: Engineering numbers from the JICA Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Project (Phase 3) Final Report, Nov 2017. Refreshed when new ADB/JICA/BWSSB documents are published; supplemented with WELL Labs + IISc Groundwater Outlook + Karnataka WRD where the picture has shifted since 2017.
_view_overrides.demand_caption: Unlike Chennai (impounded local reservoirs) and Madurai (gravity feed from Mullaperiyar), Bangalore is fundamentally a pumped city. Up to 1,460 MLD is lifted ~95 km uphill from the Cauvery River via 3-stage pumping (TK Halli -> Harohalli -> Tataguni) against ~500 m elevation. JICA's 2049 demand projection of 3,456 MLD against post-Stage-V supply of 2,735 MLD opens a structural 721 MLD deficit. Bangalore's groundwater and tanker market exist because BWSSB cannot deliver enough Cauvery to meet demand.

_data_provenance_caveats: JICA Phase 3 was published November 2017 - numbers reflect 2015-2017 system state. Stage V (775 MLD design) was 'planned' in JICA and commissioned 16 October 2024 at TK Halli. Per The Ken (May 2026), Stage V actual delivery as of Feb 2026 is ~400 MLD, well below the 775 MLD design.
STP count and capacity have ~doubled since JICA's 14 plants / 721 MLD (2017) to ~39 plants / 1,371 MLD (2024-25, BWSSB on OpenCity).

GBA replaced BBMP on 15 May 2025 (Karnataka Act 36 of 2025). Final 369-ward delimitation notified 19 Nov 2025. JICA used BBMP's 198-ward Core area + 8 ULBs + 110 villages structure - geometry has shifted; functional supply chain is unchanged.

Groundwater extraction: BWSSB official 800 MLD in JICA-era assumptions; WELL Labs Bengaluru Urban Water Balance (Jan 2024) bottom-up estimate is 1,392 MLD. Both documented in current_supply_mix_mld and groundwater section.
JICA flagged NRW at 48% in 2017. BWSSB UFW reduction projects have run since; current NRW is not officially published.

Cauvery release variability: JICA Figure 6.1 shows daily flow at Kollegal Point 1972-2016. Even drought year 2012 met Stage I-IV requirements. Stage V demand pushes total close to the safe-yield envelope.

current_supply_mix_mld.note: WELL Labs Jan 2024 bottom-up urban water balance. 592 MLD HIGHER than BWSSB's official number. The divergence IS the story.

_supply_total_note: 1,310 MLD is the operational Cauvery WTP capacity across Stages I-IV (JICA Phase 3 Table 3.1 + Salient Features Table 3.1.2). NOT including Stage V's reported ~400 MLD actual delivery, NOT including the contested ~800-1,392 MLD groundwater layer. JICA-era monthly maximum supply was 1,450 MLD (which used some allocation buffer); monthly average was 1,390 MLD. Pre-Stage-V baseline.

wtps_summary._note: Multi-WTP shape (same shape Chennai uses). The 5 Cauvery 'stages' are physically co-located at TK Halli WTP complex but commissioned across different years with different treatment processes. Total installed = 1,310 MLD (Stages I-IV) + 775 MLD (Stage V design) = 2,085 MLD design capacity; actual Stage V delivery is ~400 MLD per The Ken May 2026 so real total is ~1,710 MLD.
wtps_summary.planned_additions_breakdown: Stage V Project (commissioned 16 Oct 2024 at TK Halli, 775 MLD design; ~400 MLD actually delivered as of Feb 2026 per The Ken). Stage V was the primary subject of the JICA Phase 3 preparatory survey.

distribution._note: Distribution figures from JICA Phase 3 Salient Features (Table 3.1.2) - 2015-2017 BWSSB snapshot. Numbers will have grown since with GBA's expansion to 369 wards across 5 corporations. GLRs map to Chennai's 'ground-level Clear Water Reservoirs' (CWRs) for the shared dashboard component.
distribution._admin_zones_note: BWSSB has 9 divisions, further split into 31 sub-divisions for O&M, billing, and collection. Each sub-division runs a service station that owns inflow metering for its area.
distribution._ground_level_cwrs_note: 84 GLRs at 51 sites totalling 1,064 ML storage. Plus 52 OHTs (45.9 ML). Pumped water from Tataguni feeds GLRs first, then gravity/pump to OHTs and direct service areas.
distribution._wdss_note: Bangalore doesn't use Chennai's WDS terminology; 51 GLR sites approximately correspond to Chennai's WDS hubs. 62 booster pumping stations + 7,477 public faucets + 371 public taps complete the last-mile network.
distribution._transmission_mains_note: Cauvery transmission spans ~95 km from TK Halli intake (12.45 N, 76.86 E) uphill to BBMP via 3-stage pumping (TK Halli -> Harohalli -> Tataguni). Total elevation gain ~500 m.

connections._total_note: Per JICA Phase 3 Salient Features (2015-2017 snapshot): 865,000 house service connections. Often cited as '~11 lakh' in 2024-era BWSSB framing - includes growth + commercial.

distribution._population_note: Per JICA Phase 3 Salient Features (2015-16 snapshot): 5.8M people served. Now ~8M+ within BBMP and ~13.5M across GBA's 369 wards (Nov 2025 delimitation). Coverage of newly-added wards is incomplete pending Stage V full delivery.

demand._note: Demand projections from JICA Phase 3 Tables 5.3 + 6.3 (high-growth population scenario; matches BBMP M/P assumption of ~20M by 2051). JICA uses CPHEEO's 150 LPCD design standard for metropolitan cities with sewerage.
demand._population_2034_note: JICA Table 5.1: Core 6.5M + ULB 4.8M + 110V 2.8M = 14.1M (2034). Includes high-growth assumption (medium scenario projects ~12M).
demand._demand_breakdown_note: JICA Table 6.3 (high pop): 2034 total water demand 2,608 MLD = 2,108 MLD piped supply + 500 MLD groundwater abstraction. 2049 demand 3,456 MLD = 2,956 + 500.
demand._demand_gap_2034_note: Post-Stage-V supply of 2,735 MLD (1,460 Cauvery + 775 Stage V + 500 GW) covers 2034 demand of 2,608 MLD with 127 MLD surplus. Headline gap is 2049, not 2034.
demand._demand_gap_2049_note: JICA Table 6.3: by 2049, post-Stage-V supply still 2,735 MLD against demand 3,456 MLD = 721 MLD structural deficit. Closing this needs either Stage VI/inter-basin transfer, an order-of-magnitude UFW reduction, or large-scale wastewater reuse + recycling. No Stage VI is currently planned.
demand._city_area_note: JICA Phase 3 BBMP composition (2017): Core 245 + 8 ULBs 330 + 110 villages 225 = 800 sq km. Post-Nov 2025 GBA delimitation reorganises into 5 City Corporations across 369 wards; total area expanded but not yet officially published.

allocation_context._note: JICA Phase 3 Table 6.1: Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal allocation by state, per Gazette No. 373 of 19 Feb 2013. 1 TMC = 77.5 MLD per JICA's working conversion.
allocation_context._state_share_note: JICA Table 6.1 cites the original Gazette notification. The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal final award (2007) + Supreme Court 2018 modification adjusts Karnataka's share within these totals.
allocation_context._basin_note: JICA 6.2.1 + India-WRIS Database. Karnataka holds 42% of the 85,626 km^2 basin (~36,000 km^2), the largest share.
allocation_context._cwss_allocation_breakdown: JICA Table 6.2: Stage I+II+III = 730 MLD (GO PWD/41MMM/04/Bengaluru, 10 Dec 1984); Stage IV Ph1+Ph2 = 730 MLD (GO HUD/MNI/90/Bengaluru, 27 July 1994); Stage V = 775 MLD (GO of Karnataka 10 TMC additional). Total 2,235 MLD = ~21% of Karnataka's 270 TMC drinking allocation.
allocation_context._energy_cost_note: Widely cited BWSSB figure (Wikipedia citation): pumping ~95 km uphill against ~500 m elevation consumes 75% of agency revenues. Single largest factor in Bangalore's water tariff structure.
allocation_context._lpcd_note: JICA Salient Features (2015-16): 146 LPCD supplied; only 76 LPCD reaching consumers. 48% NRW gap.
allocation_context._nrw_note: JICA Phase 3 Salient Features Table 3.1.2. UFW targets (Table 6.3.5): Core+ULB to drop from 23% (2017) to 16% (2049); 110 Villages steady at 16%. Current actual NRW not officially re-published since 2017.
allocation_context._cauvery_flow_note: JICA Table 6.2.5: 1972-2016 Cauvery flow at Kollegal Point. Drought-year average is 2,539 MLD vs the post-Stage V intake requirement of 2,235 MLD - a 304 MLD margin against a high baseline year. Stage VI would erode this further.

upstream_dams._note: JICA Phase 3 Table 6.2.6: the 4 Cauvery basin reservoirs whose combined live storage gates BWSSB's annual supply security. These are tracked in neer-vazhvu's water_sources table for Bangalore.
upstream_dams._equivalent_note: 2,583 Mm^3 / 365 days = ~7,000 MLD/day if drawn evenly across a year. BWSSB's 2,235 MLD intake requirement post-Stage V is ~32% of this. But the dams also serve irrigation (Mandya, Mysore) and downstream Tamil Nadu obligations under CWDT - drinking water gets a slice, not the whole envelope.

tertiary_treatment._note: JICA Phase 3 Tables 6.3.3 + 6.3.4: tertiary treatment plants beyond secondary STPs. Bangalore already produces ~161 MLD of tertiary-treated reuse water - more than commonly cited.

plants.name: KPTCL power-plant supply
plants.use: Karnataka Power Transmission Corp - power plant cooling

tertiary_treatment._implication: JICA notes treated sewage cannot be mixed with domestic supply under current policy, but is increasingly displacing industrial freshwater demand. TG Halli IPR pilot (with SUEZ, 110 MLD design) would be a major expansion of this layer if it succeeds.

groundwater_expert_committee_2017._note: JICA Phase 3 Section 6.3: Bengaluru Groundwater Expert Committee's findings on aquifer extraction. A third data point between BWSSB's official 800 MLD framing and WELL Labs' 2024 bottom-up 1,392 MLD estimate.
groundwater_expert_committee_2017._committee_findings: At present approximately 570 MLD is being extracted from the deep aquifer in Core+ULB (Water Source Expert Report). For future planning the committee recommended assuming 400 MLD continued from this source plus 100 MLD for 110 villages. The committee's 500 MLD total (used in JICA Table 6.3 water balance) sits below BWSSB's 800 MLD official and well below WELL Labs' 1,392 MLD. All three numbers should be cited together; the divergence reflects what is officially planned-for vs what is actually extracted vs what is sustainably available.

rainfall_harvesting_potential._note: JICA Phase 3 Section 6.3 + rainwater study: theoretical maximum of urban rainwater harvesting across the 800 sq km BBMP catchment.
rainfall_harvesting_potential._implication: JICA notes rainwater can't be mixed with domestic supply under current policy, but Karnataka mandates rainwater-harvesting installation in new buildings (>40x60 ft sites). The 613-690 MLD harvestable potential is ~3-4x the current tertiary treatment capacity - a structurally large under-utilised supply source.

project_cost._note: JICA Phase 3 Table 16.2.1 + 16.2.2: project cost estimate for the JICA Survey scope (the Stage V WTP + 110 villages sewerage). At 2017 prices.
project_cost._funding_note: 85% JICA loan / 7.5% Government of Karnataka / 7.5% BWSSB. Stage V was commissioned 16 Oct 2024 at TK Halli (~7 years from JICA Phase 3 Final Report). Per The Ken May 2026, actual delivery is ~400 MLD against 775 MLD design - a Rs 4,435 crore investment running at ~52% of installed capacity.

household_economics._note: JICA Phase 3 Chapter 14 social survey: household-level economics across BBMP. Anchors the affordability + willingness-to-pay question.
household_economics._water_connection_willingness: 77.5% of respondents ready to pay below INR 500 for water connection fee; 21.6% ready for INR 500-1,000; remainder above INR 1,000.
household_economics._sewerage_connection_willingness: 85.7% of respondents ready to pay below INR 300 for sewerage connection.
household_economics._implication: JICA found that ~78% of BBMP households tolerated connection costs below INR 500 - meaning major upfront cost recovery is not viable. BWSSB's revenue model is therefore monthly tariff + bulk-supply pricing, not connection charges. The 24%/54% willingness-to-pay split for monthly tariff suggests an INR 500 ceiling per household for piped + sewerage service is the political affordability floor.

stress_wards_iisc._note: From IISc Groundwater Outlook of Bengaluru City (April 2025), BWSSB-commissioned, names 65 specific wards as 'over-exploited' on the CGWB framework. Mapped to the pre-Nov 2025 BBMP 198-ward configuration; mapping to GBA 369 wards is a follow-up.
stress_wards_iisc.stress_ward_implication: Per BWSSB's own commissioned study, ~33% of BBMP wards operate beyond CGWB's 'safe' groundwater extraction limit. Cauvery Stage V was meant to relieve these wards via piped supply; under-delivery means many remain on groundwater + tankers.

tanker_market._note: Bangalore's informal water market is uniquely large among Indian metros. JICA Phase 3 noted 62 BWSSB tanker lorries in 2017; the private tanker fleet is multiples of that.
tanker_market.official_app: Kaveriwheels (BWSSB-operated, ~19K downloads in a 14M city as of 2026, 2.8/5 rating)
tanker_market.informal_rate_note: Crisis-peak summer 2024 rates. Off-season tankers are ~Rs 800-1,200 per 6-12kL but rates surge 2-4x when piped supply fails.

stps._note: JICA Phase 3 Table 4.1 documented 14 STPs / 721 MLD in 2017. Current state (per OpenCity BWSSB STP dataset 2024-25) is ~39 STPs / 1,371 MLD - capacity roughly DOUBLED post-JICA. Headline STPs from the 2017 inventory below; the 2024-25 inventory lives in public/geojson/bangalore-stps.geojson.

tg_halli_reuse_project._note: TG Halli reservoir is BWSSB's defunct 1933 surface impoundment on the Arkavathi river (Chamarajasagara). Since the 1990s the upstream sewage burden killed it as a drinking source. The BWSSB-SUEZ Indirect Potable Reuse (IPR) project repurposes it as a 110 MLD STP-blended reuse reservoir - the country's largest IPR pilot.
tg_halli_reuse_project.scheme: STP-treated wastewater blended in TG Halli reservoir for indirect potable reuse

reference_figures.caption: JICA Phase 3 supply chain: Cauvery River -> SBR -> NBR -> MS pipelines -> TK Halli WTP (Stages I-V) -> 3-stage pumping (TK Halli -> Harohalli -> Tataguni) -> 84 GLRs -> 52 OHTs -> distribution. JICA Phase 3 Figure 3.x.

Cauvery 355-day flow at Kollegal Point 1972-2016 plotted against Stage I-IV + Stage V intake requirements. Even drought-year 2012 maintained sufficient flow for Stages I-IV; Stage V demand pushes against safe-yield envelope.

Water balance 2024 / 2034 / 2049: supply (Cauvery + Stage V + groundwater + UFW savings + tertiary treated + rainwater) vs demand by area (Core + ULB + 110 villages). 2049 shows a structural 721 MLD deficit.
